name: API Layer
description: Describes the HTTP API surface the application exposes or consumes: the API document and its servers, paths and operations, parameters, request bodies and responses, media types, headers, links and callbacks, reusable components and schemas, security schemes and webhooks (OpenAPI 3.0). Route handlers, controllers and generated API clients are evidence for elements here; the application behaviour behind an operation belongs to the application layer. Modelling rules: each API object links only to what its OpenAPI 3.0 fields hold, and every nesting in the document tree is composes: the document composes its info, paths, components, servers and tags; paths compose path items, and a path item composes its operations, parameters and servers; an operation composes its parameters, request body, responses map, callbacks and servers; the responses map composes its responses, and a response composes its headers, media types and links; a media type composes its schema, examples and encodings; a server composes its variables, a security scheme its OAuth flows, and components their reusable entries. Reuse through $ref is references, and allOf inheritance is specializes. A rate limit, which OpenAPI does not define, governs the operations, path items and servers it caps, triggers its 429 response, references the headers and security scheme it counts by, and realizes its countermeasure. An operation realizes the application function it exposes and references its application service, and a document realizes its application service; the API reaches the business layer through the application layer. A security scheme realizes the security policy it applies, requires permissions and references the secure resource it protects. API schemas reach data stores and business objects through the data-model schemas that map to them. An operation satisfies requirements and constraints, supports the goals and outcomes it contributes to, and realizes the countermeasures it implements.
